perspectives.name: discovery-weak-signals
observations: Kinder Morgan's Q2 2026 backlog was $9.6 billion, with about 92% in natural-gas projects and more than 60% tied to power-generation and local-distribution demand.

The Amarillo Expansion is being developed partly for Texas Panhandle data-center demand; its planned capacity is fully subscribed under a long-term contract, linking AI/data-center power growth to incremental gas infrastructure demand.

perspectives.name: expectations-execution
observations: KMI placed about $660 million of expansion projects into service during Q2 2026 while generating $2.0 billion cash flow from operations and $1.0 billion free cash flow after capex.
Q2 net income rose 21% year over year, and management said it can fund virtually all backlog internally; execution evidence is therefore stronger than a purely prospective backlog narrative.

risks: Pipeline projects remain exposed to permitting and construction timing.
Long-lived gas infrastructure faces policy, demand-transition and commodity-adjacent risks despite fee-based contracts.
Backlog does not guarantee all contingent projects reach service.
unknowns: Project-by-project realized returns versus planned economics remain unverified here.
Long-run durability of incremental data-center gas demand is uncertain.
